recent_signals.headline: **THE HELIUM SHORTAGE IS A STRUCTURAL MULTI-YEAR DEFICIT, NOT A SPIKE — and the 8-12 WEEK LAG means the March/April rationing lands in shipments NOW.** ~30-35% of global supply remains offline at Ras Laffan with a **3-5 YEAR repair timeline** (helium is a byproduct of LNG liquefaction, so the trains that make LNG make the helium — the Qatari LNG outage and the helium outage are the same event). Dependence is higher than headlines suggest: **Korea imports 64.7% of its helium from Qatar (higher for 6N ultra-pure grade); Taiwan ~69% from the GCC.** Ultra-pure helium prices have DOUBLED since March; there is no exchange price, only a contract market. Samsung and SK Hynix are running conservation protocols — non-critical use cut, high-value lines prioritised, safety stock drawn down, sourcing from the US and Russia — but **NEITHER has announced a formal production cut.** TSMC says it expects no significant near-term impact, citing diversified contracts and on-site recycling capex that the Korean memory fabs lack. **THE ANALYTICAL POINT THE GRAPH SHOULD CARRY: the standing thesis treats KOSPI as a demand-side AI bear market, which is probably right — but the helium channel means memory SUPPLY is also constrained, and a supply-constrained memory market inside a demand downturn is an unusual configuration that should not be modelled as a pure demand story.** CONFIRMED.

Status unchanged: **~30-35% of global supply offline at Ras Laffan with a 3-5 year repair horizon**, Korea 64.7% Qatar-dependent and Taiwan ~69% GCC-dependent, ultra-pure prices reported up sharply (no dated spot print obtainable — the '+50%' figure is CLAIMED and undated). **THE KEY NEGATIVE FINDING: no production cut has been announced by Samsung, SK Hynix or TSMC.** The 8-12 week rationing-to-shipment lag implies March/April constraints should be landing in July-September shipments; they have not yet appeared as announced output reductions. **This is now a test the thesis is beginning to fail on timing** — either conservation protocols and safety stock are absorbing more than modelled, or the effect is showing up in yield and cost rather than in headline output.
